intro: A scaled error compares a forecast with the typical error of a seasonal-naive training baseline. Using evaluation observations to estimate that baseline would leak information into the reference scale.
task: Normalize evaluation absolute error by training seasonal-naive absolute error with an explicit zero-scale policy.
requirements: lag is an integer in 1..len(training)-1. actual and predicted are equal-length evaluation vectors.
scale=mean(abs(training[lag:]-training[:-lag])); return {"scale": scalar, "mae": mean evaluation absolute error, "mase": mae/scale}.
If scale is zero and mae is zero, use mase=0. If scale is zero and mae is positive, raise ValueError because a finite relative score is undefined.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

hints.body: Estimate the naive-error scale only from the training series.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: Measure evaluation MAE separately, then apply the documented zero-scale convention.

explanation: A scaled error compares a forecast with the typical error of a seasonal-naive training baseline. Using evaluation observations to estimate that baseline would leak information into the reference scale.

The ratio is unit-free, but a perfectly constant seasonal training series has zero baseline error. A positive error cannot then be represented by a finite ratio, so the contract rejects that case explicitly.
